QF.id: I Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_59

question.text: When is a clearing member put into "Risk Reduction Mode" by the Stock Exchange / Clearing Corporation?

answer.text: When 90% of the stock broker's/clearing member's collateral available for margin adjustment is utilised
When 75% of the clearing member's collateral is utilised
When the clearing member's margin shortfall exceeds Rs. 1 crore
When the clearing member breaches 100% of their collateral utilisation

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 178 says stock brokers must be put in risk-reduction mode when a specified percent (currently 90%) of the stock broker's/clearing member's collateral available for adjustment against margins gets utilised. The Trap: The 90% trigger is the workbook number; lower thresholds such as 75% and bespoke shortfall rupee amounts are not the source-defined trigger. Note: Once in risk-reduction mode, unexecuted orders are cancelled, only IOC orders are permitted, and position-increasing orders are checked for margin sufficiency before acceptance.
